decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “Save a bookmark: add a link by its address.”
decisions.note: The initial specification conforms to URL-based bookmark creation at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “a title is auto-derived if none is given” and “Stores references only”; R1 client: “Automatic page details when saving: title, description, favicon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: The proposed metadata behavior omitted automatic collection of the required page details; the client supplied the conforming behavior at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker offered optional title/description and later “rename”; R1 client required automatic details “while still letting me edit the title and description.”
decisions.note: The original presentation did not establish editable auto-collected title and description both before and after saving; the client explicitly corrected it.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker defined editing as “rename, re-tag”; R5 maker again only explicitly reported “title/description editable.” Neither R1 nor R5 client response mentions editing a bookmark’s URL.
decisions.note: The presented edit scope omitted URL editing, and the client never surfaced that difference.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “delete bookmarks (with a delete confirmation).”
decisions.note: Permanent deletion was included and conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker’s save/edit stories did not address duplicate URLs; R1 client: “Duplicate addresses should take me to edit the existing bookmark rather than create another copy.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing duplicate-save convergence rule at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker only described “Browse and find”; R2 maker specified that the preview image is “a thumbnail shown in the list,” and R2 client confirmed the list thumbnail, but no presentation establishes whether every list item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon.
decisions.note: A list presentation was discussed, but the evidence cannot establish either full conformance or a definite divergence in its readability fields.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker included optional tags when saving and “re-tag” when editing; R1 client: “Tags are enough.”
decisions.note: Assignment and later modification of tags conform to the tagging requirement.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented optional tag entry and re-tagging; R1 client said only “Tags are enough.” No maker or client entry addresses existing-tag autocomplete.
decisions.note: Tag entry is in scope, but its autocomplete behavior cannot be established from the record.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “filter by tag”; R5 maker confirmed “tag filter.”
decisions.note: Selecting a tag-based filter conforms to the reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker limited keyword search to “title/address/description/tags,” omitting notes; R1 client requested saved notes but did not state that notes must be searched.
decisions.note: The initial search-field decision omitted note content, and the client did not explicitly surface that search difference.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker proposed “search by keyword”; R5 maker reported keyword search over several fields. No entry specifies whether matching is case-insensitive, and the client’s final approval does not clarify it.
decisions.note: The search decision lacks enough evidence to determine its case-sensitivity.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented keyword search plus a separate tag filter; R5 maker reported keyword search over tags. Neither presentation nor client response addresses `#tag` query syntax.
decisions.note: The record cannot establish whether hashtag search is supported or deliberately omitted.

decisions.evidence: R1 and R5 maker entries describe keyword search but do not state whether AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, or quoted literal operators are supported; the client does not clarify this.
decisions.note: Boolean-search behavior remains indeterminate rather than a confirmed divergence.

decisions.evidence: R1 and R5 maker entries describe keyword search but never specify exact quoted-phrase matching; the client does not address it.
decisions.note: Exact-phrase behavior cannot be established from the presentation or response.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker’s three stories omitted read state; R1 client requested “Read later” status and “a separate unread view.” R5 maker later delivered a “read/unread toggle + dedicated Unread view.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing read-state workflow at the specification gate; the linked later presentation confirms the intended two-state behavior.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker asked whether “sorting options” were missing; R1 client required “Sorting, at least by date added and title.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing sorting requirement and concrete sort keys.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker’s bookmark fields and edit story omitted notes; R1 client: “I also expect saved notes.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing ability to write and retain bookmark notes at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker revised the feature to “Saved notes”; R5 maker described “Free-form notes, searchable.” The R2 and R5 client approvals do not state whether notes use Markdown or render as Markdown.
decisions.note: The revised note decision resolves note storage but leaves the reference’s Markdown authoring/rendering semantics unestablished through implementation review.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “Stores references only — it does not fetch/archive page content”; R1 client required “a preserved page snapshot, including keeping PDFs as PDFs.”
decisions.note: The client replaced the explicit references-only behavior with the required local snapshot and PDF rule.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker proposed app-local storage and no page archiving; after local snapshots were added, R3 maker still specified storage as “all local, durable across restarts, no external service.” R3 client approved MHTML/PDF snapshots without identifying the missing Internet Archive option.
decisions.note: The specification/plan explicitly confines preservation to local storage, excluding Internet Archive snapshots; the client never surfaces that difference.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker offered deletion but no bookmark archive workflow; R1 client required “Reversible archiving with its own archive view, distinct from permanent deletion.”
decisions.note: The client supplied all three related archive requirements at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “Import/export ... are out of scope for v1”; R1 client: “I would like standard bookmark import/export in v1.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly rejected the proposed exclusion and placed both standard import and export in v1.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker revised the spec to auto-collect “title, description, favicon, preview image” with editable title/description; R2 client approved. R5 maker reported the same behavior as delivered.
decisions.note: The revised specification and implementation conform to automatic metadata collection and editing.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker added preserved snapshots with PDFs kept as PDFs; R2 client accepted “a faithful static snapshot.” R3 selected single-file MHTML and original PDF bytes, which the client approved.
decisions.note: MHTML is a functionally equivalent single-file static web snapshot, while PDF passthrough exactly matches the reference rule.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker added “Read-later status + unread view”; R5 maker delivered a “read/unread toggle + dedicated Unread view,” and R5 client accepted the app.
decisions.note: The revised and implemented read-state workflow conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker added “Reversible archive + archive view, distinct from delete”; R5 maker delivered reversible archive, a separate Archive view, and permanent delete.
decisions.note: The revised archive workflow conforms to all three archive requirements.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker added sort by date added and title in both directions; R5 maker reported date/title ascending and descending sorting.
decisions.note: The revised sorting decision conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker specified “Duplicate address → edit existing, not a copy,” including archived duplicates; R3 planned lookup across active and archived records; R5 reported it delivered.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate handling conforms and is stricter across archived records.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker stated saved notes were “also searchable”; R5 maker reported keyword search across “title/address/description/notes/tags.”
decisions.note: The revised field coverage includes all full-text fields required by the reference.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker defined the standard browser HTML bookmark format; R2 client explicitly approved it. R3 and R5 identify it as standard Netscape bookmark HTML export.
decisions.note: The selected export format conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker proposed standard browser HTML import with nested folders mapped to tags, which R2 client approved; R5 maker reported Netscape HTML import and folders-to-tags, but no entry establishes preservation of the original date-added value.
decisions.note: The import format and tag mapping are resolved, but required date-added preservation cannot be established from the record.
